chunks: The Knowledge of Allah, the Exalted:

Surely, Allah, the Glorified, nothing is hidden from Him of whatever people do in their nights or days. He knows all the details, and His knowledge covers them. Your limbs are a witness, the organs of your body constitute an army (against yourself), your inner self serves Him as eyes (to watch your sins), and your loneliness is open to Him.
ai.seo_question: How does Islam describe God's knowledge of human actions in private and public?
ai.summary: In this passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) elucidates the attribute of Allah's comprehensive knowledge (Ilm) by employing a sophisticated anthropomorphic metaphor where the body's limbs and faculties act as divine witnesses. This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of the integration between external actions and internal states (batin), emphasizing that accountability is not merely observational but inherent in the very structure of the human being. The text underscores the concept of 'Ilm al-Dhātī' (God's knowledge by essence) extending to all minute details of creation, reinforcing the spiritual discipline of 'Muraqaba' (mindfulness of God).
